US9298709B2
A patent publication titled "Computer system to visualize data from an IP rights database," describing a data processing system for visualizing IP rights data on a geographic map.

Data Processing System
A computer system (10) that visualizes data from an IP rights database as a geographic map with a viewable area, generating and updating data visualizations based on the current map coordinates and restriction criteria.<SEP>A system having one or more processors and memory configured to evaluate information via a computer network, including receiving user interest indications, determining keyword weights, ranking keywords, and selecting advertisements.<SEP>A computer-based system that detects user interest, identifies keywords, determines keyword weights, receives content requests, ranks keywords, and selects content for display with information resources.

IP Rights Database
A database containing intellectual property rights records, including geographic addresses of IP right owners, used as the source for generating lists of IP rights.<SEP>A database containing IP rights records, including geographic addresses of IP right owners, from which lists of IP rights are generated and restricted.

Geographic Map
A displayed geographic map having a viewable area whose geographic coordinates define the geographic area used to filter IP rights by owner address.

Map Display Change Monitor
A component (23) that receives and stores geographic coordinates of the viewable area, compares current with previously stored coordinates, and generates a display change notification, including after a pre-defined time period with no change.

Display Change Notification
A notification issued upon detecting a change in the viewable area of the geographic map, generated after a pre-defined time period elapses with no change in the viewable area.<SEP>A notification generated by the map display change monitor including the geographic coordinates of the current viewable area of the geographic map.

IP Rights List Generator
A component (37) that generates a list of IP rights from the IP rights database whose owner's geographic address falls within the current map area, and restricts the list based on restriction criteria to form a restricted list.

Restriction Criteria Interface
A component that ascertains one or more restriction criteria related to the IP rights used to restrict the list of IP rights.

Restriction Criteria
Criteria related to IP rights used to restrict a list of IP rights, including IP jurisdiction, type of IP right, technology type, industry type, filing date, number of applications, owner type, representative listing, IPC classes, and trademark classes.<SEP>Criteria related to IP rights used to restrict the list, including IP jurisdiction, type of IP right, technology type, industry type, filing date, owner filing count, owner type, representative listing, IPC classes, and trademark classes.

Restricted List Of IP Rights
A list of IP rights filtered from the IP rights database based on one or more restriction criteria related to the IP rights.<SEP>A list of IP rights filtered by geographic area of owner address and by one or more restriction criteria, from which data visualizations are derived.

Information Display Generator
A component that generates and displays an information pane containing data visualizations derived from a restricted list of IP rights, updating them based on geographic co-ordinates of the current viewable area.<SEP>A component (26) that generates and displays an information pane containing data visualizations derived from the restricted list of IP rights and updates them upon each successive display change notification.

Information Pane
A display area containing one or more data visualizations related to a restricted list of IP rights.<SEP>A displayed pane containing one or more data visualizations derived from the restricted list of IP rights.

Data Visualization
Visual representations generated in the information pane from the restricted list of IP rights, including technology type charts, industry type charts, filing trend analysis charts, owner filing size charts, and lists of IP rights owners.<SEP>Visualizations derived from the restricted list of IP rights, such as technology type charts, industry type charts, filing trend analysis charts, and IP rights owner filing size charts.

Data Visualization Selector
A component that allows the user to select one or more data visualizations based on the restriction criteria.

Geographic Map Display Interface
An interface that displays a geographic map having a viewable area.

IP Right Owner
An individual or corporation owning one or more IP rights, whose geographic address is used to determine inclusion within a geographic area.<SEP>An owner of an IP right whose geographic address is used to determine whether the IP right falls within the current viewable map area; may be an individual or a corporation.

User History Of Use
A history of use of the system provided by storing geographic coordinates of the viewable area for an entire session or multiple sessions.

IPC Classes
Defined International Patent Classification classes used as a restriction criterion for classifying patent IP rights.<SEP>Defined International Patent Classification classes used as a restriction criterion for patent IP rights.

Filing Trend Analysis Chart
A data visualization chart showing filing trend analysis for the IP rights.

IP Rights Owner Filing Size Chart
A data visualization chart showing the filing size of IP rights owners.

Geographic Map Display
A display component showing a geographic map with a viewable area defined by geographic co-ordinates, used to spatially filter IP rights by owner address.

Map Change Message
A message generated in relation to a change in the viewable area of the geographic map, generated after a pre-defined time period elapses and there has been no change in the viewable area.

IP Rights
Intellectual property rights, such as patents and trademarks, that are listed, restricted, and visualized based on owner geographic addresses and restriction criteria.

Geographic Co-Ordinates
Coordinates defining the current viewable area of the geographic map display, used to determine the geographic area for filtering IP rights and to update data visualizations.

User Initiated Command
A command initiated by a user, such as pressing an on-screen button, that triggers generation or updating of data visualizations.

On-Screen Button
A button displayed on screen that a user presses to initiate a command for updating data visualizations.

Trademark Classes
Defined classes used as a restriction criterion for classifying trademark IP rights.

US8509827B2
A patent publication titled "Methods and apparatus of context-data acquisition and ranking" that discloses a system, method, and article of manufacture for acquiring and ranking context data based on a query derived from a short message.

Context-Data Acquisition And Ranking
A method of determining a context-data type from a query, identifying context-data sources, generating requests for context data, and ranking received context data according to a specified parameter.

Context-Data Type
A classification of context data determined algorithmically from the meaning of a term of a short message, providing information about the environment or context of a mobile device.

Context-Data Source
A provider that supplies context data of a given context-data type and can be ranked according to a specified parameter such as pecuniary cost.

Short Message
A message whose content has a meaning to which context-data is related, and to which relevant context data is linked.<SEP>A message received from a mobile device, whose term meanings are used to determine a context-data type and to which received context data may be appended or encoded.

Mobile Device
A device that generates a short message and a query, and to which received context data may be provided; may be a smart phone.<SEP>A portable device including at least a camera and a screen, running an application in operative communication with the camera and an Internet access mechanism. It may be a mobile phone, tablet, PDA, or dedicated camera.<SEP>A device including at least a camera and a screen, used to interact with a social networking service; may be a mobile phone, tablet, PDA, or dedicated camera.

Server
At least one server associated with a context-data provider used to collect a set of context-data.<SEP>A computing system that receives short messages from mobile devices, determines context-data types, identifies and ranks context-data sources, and generates requests for context data.<SEP>A computing system that receives requests, traverses social networks to identify connecting persons, and sends identifiers or responses to the requesting person's computer.<SEP>A server hosted by the computing device that performs the typographical error classification operations.<SEP>A computing system that streams video content features to a client.<SEP>A server that receives data comprising characteristics of e-mail exchanges from the interaction database, assigns weights to characteristics, and transfers data to a processor.<SEP>A server that receives data comprising characteristics of e-mail exchanges, assigns weights to characteristics, and transfers data to a processor for generating relationship data.

Specified Parameter
A criterion used to rank context-data sources, comprising a pecuniary cost to acquire context data, a state of the receiving mobile device, a state of an available communication network, or a cost value of the context data.

Recipient Mobile Device
A mobile device that receives context data, possibly associated with or appended to a short message, or a URI of a database server.

Database
A storage system available to a recipient mobile device in which received context data may be stored and queried via metadata instructions.<SEP>A storage that holds a plurality of keywords and their associated weights, associated with a parked domain web page having a unique identifier.<SEP>A storage system from which keywords of advertisements are identified using the unique identifier of the parked domain web page and in which increased keyword weights are associated with the parked domain web page.<SEP>A searchable database in which management data is stored in a searchable format.<SEP>A searchable storage repository in which extracted management data is stored for subsequent review and query by users and administrators.<SEP>A searchable database in which the management data is stored in a searchable format.<SEP>A searchable storage system in which management data is stored.

Uniform Resource Identifier
An identifier of a database server that may be forwarded to a receiving mobile device.

Markup Language
A language used to encode received context data into a short message.

Computerized-Apparatus
An apparatus comprising at least one memory with program instructions and at least one processor configured to execute operations for context-data acquisition and ranking.

Computer Readable Medium
A medium comprising computer-executable instructions adapted to perform the context-data acquisition and ranking method.

Physical Sensor
A device by which the context-data is obtained.<SEP>A sensor by which context data related to the meaning of short message content is obtained.

Context-Data Provider
An entity with at least one server that collects and provides a set of context-data, and is allowed to provide a cost of the context-data.<SEP>A provider from which a set of context data related to the meaning of short message content is collected by a server.

Metric
A measure used to algorithmically select relevant context data, comprising a monetary cost of the context-data.<SEP>A measure according to which relevant context data is algorithmically selected, comprising a monetary cost of the context-data.

Smart Phone
A type of mobile device that may generate the short message.

Communication Network
A network through which context data may be communicated to a mobile device and whose state may serve as a specified parameter.<SEP>A network over which queries are received and responses transmitted electronically; may be the Internet.<SEP>A network such as the Internet over which queries are received electronically and responses are transmitted electronically to a party.<SEP>A network over which queries are received and responses transmitted electronically, which may be the Internet.

Context-Data
Data related to the meaning of a short message content, obtained by a physical sensor and provided by context-data providers, weighted and selected according to at least one metric.

Monetary Cost
The cost of the context-data, used as a metric for selecting relevant context data.

Communication Protocol
A protocol according to which the relevant context data and the short message are formatted, such as a cellular network short message protocol or an internet communication protocol.

Cellular Network Short Message Protocol
A communication protocol comprising a cellular network short message protocol.

Internet Communication Protocol
A communication protocol comprising an internet communication protocol.

Device
The device that generated the short message and has a physical context to which the context data is related.

Speaker Identification Using Hash-Based Indexing
A patent (US9514753B2) describing methods, systems, and apparatus for performing speaker identification using hash-based indexing of speaker vectors.

Utterance Vector
A vector derived from an utterance, used as a query for comparing against speaker vectors.<SEP>A vector derived from an utterance, used as the query representation in speaker identification; may be an i-vector or based on deep neural network activations.

Speaker Vector
A vector derived from one or more utterances of a respective speaker, used to characterize the speech of that speaker.<SEP>A vector derived from one or more utterances of a respective speaker, stored in hash tables and compared against an utterance vector to identify a speaker.

Hash Values
Values determined for an utterance vector according to multiple different hash functions, used to retrieve candidate speaker vectors from hash tables.

Hash Tables
A plurality of tables storing speaker vectors, indexed by hash values, from which a set of candidate speaker vectors is determined.

Hash Functions
Multiple different functions used to compute hash values for vectors; may include locality sensitive hash functions and hyperplane-based hashing.

Locality Sensitive Hash Functions
A type of hash function used to determine hash values such that similar vectors are likely to hash to similar values.

Hyperplanes
Geometric constructs used to determine hash values based on the position of an utterance vector relative to different hyperplanes.

I-Vector
A vector comprising parameters determined using multivariate factor analysis of an utterance or of one or more utterances of a respective speaker.<SEP>A vector comprising parameters determined using multivariate factor analysis of an utterance or of one or more utterances of a speaker.

Deep Neural Network
A neural network whose activations, occurring in response to information about an utterance, are used to determine vector parameters.

Similarity Scores
Scores each indicating a degree of similarity between the utterance vector and one of the speaker vectors in the set, used to select the most similar speaker vector.

Cosine Distance
A measure of distance between the utterance vector and each speaker vector in the set, used to determine similarity scores.

Maximum Distance Threshold Value
A threshold against which the smallest cosine distance is compared to decide whether to select a speaker vector.

Speaker Identity
Data indicating the identity of a speaker, determined based on associations between speaker vectors and respective speakers.<SEP>The identity of a speaker determined from the selected speaker vector and output as data.

Media Items
Media items that include utterances of a speaker corresponding to the selected speaker vector and can be identified and output.

Video Resources
A set of multiple video resources from which speaker vectors are generated.

User Authentication
A process of authenticating a particular user based at least in part on determining that the selected speaker vector corresponds to that user.

Speaker
A person whose speech characteristics are represented by a speaker vector and who may be identified via a speaker identity.<SEP>A person whose utterances are represented by speaker vectors and whose identity is to be determined from an utterance.

Hash Table
A data structure among a plurality of hash tables from which speaker vectors are determined using hash values.

Hash Value
A value determined for an utterance vector according to multiple different hash functions, used to look up speaker vectors in hash tables.

Hash Function
One of multiple different hash functions used to determine hash values for an utterance vector.

Utterance
A spoken input from which an utterance vector is derived.

Multivariate Factor Analysis
A technique used to determine parameters of utterance i-vectors and speaker i-vectors.

Video Resource
A video resource for which a speaker vector is generated, among a set of multiple video resources.

Computer-Readable Storage Device
A device storing instructions that, when executed by one or more computers, cause the computers to perform operations for speaker identification.<SEP>A storage device with an executable program stored thereon that instructs a processor to perform the filtration method.<SEP>A storage device containing executable program code for presenting digital media content, establishing user relationships, and determining relevancy weights, as described in claims 13-16.

Computer
A computing machine that executes stored instructions to perform operations.

System
A system comprising one or more computers and a computer-readable storage device storing instructions.<SEP>A computing system comprising one or more processors configured to interact with a computer-readable medium to perform query pattern mining operations.<SEP>A system comprising one or more processors configured to execute computer program instructions and computer storage media encoded with such instructions.<SEP>A system that performs operations including causing display of updated content in a user interface element and inserting content into a display environment.

US9304738B1
A patent document titled "Systems and methods for selecting content using weighted terms" describing techniques for evaluating information via a computer network using weighted keywords.

Parked Domain Web Page
A web page with a unique identifier that lacks content having keywords other than content provided via the data processing system, and on which advertisements are displayed.<SEP>A web page with a unique identifier that lacks content with keywords other than content provided via the data processing system, used to display advertisements.<SEP>A web page displayed on a parked domain that shows advertisements and content selected based on ranked keywords.

Keyword
A term associated with advertisements displayed on a parked domain web page, having a weight determined based on user interest and historic performance.<SEP>A term associated with subject matter of an information resource or advertisement, assigned a weight used for content selection.<SEP>A term from a plurality of keywords that carries a weight on the parked domain web page and a different weight on a second information resource, and is used for ranking and advertisement selection.<SEP>Keywords of the data files of the data-stream, obtained by indexing types of data, included in the management data.

Weight
A value assigned to a keyword based on user interest indications and historic performance, used to rank and select keywords.<SEP>A value determined for each keyword of an information resource based on user interest indications and historic performance, used to rank and select keywords.<SEP>A value applied to each recommender, which may be site-specific, user-specific, user segment-specific, or default, and is adjusted based on user-generated events.<SEP>A value assigned to each of the plurality of characteristics for each pair of users, used to determine relationship strength.

Advertisement
An advertisement displayed with a parked domain web page, associated with one or more keywords and selected for display based on keyword weights.<SEP>Content displayed on a parked domain web page, associated with keywords and selected for display based on ranked keywords.

First Advertisement
An advertisement displayed with a parked domain web page, associated with a first keyword and in which the first user indicates interest.<SEP>An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page that a first user showed interest in, associated with a first keyword.<SEP>An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page, distinct from the second and third advertisements.

Second Advertisement
An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page, associated with a second keyword and in which the second user indicates interest.<SEP>An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page that a second user showed interest in, associated with a second keyword.<SEP>An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page, associated with the second keyword, in which the second user indicated interest.

Third Advertisement
An advertisement selected to provide for display with the parked domain web page based on the first keyword selected as the highest ranked keyword, different from the first and second advertisements.<SEP>An advertisement selected for display with the parked domain web page based on the first keyword ranked highest, different from the first and second advertisements.<SEP>An advertisement selected to be provided for display with the parked domain web page based at least in part on the first keyword selected as the highest ranked keyword, different from the first and second advertisements.

Fourth Advertisement
An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page associated with the first keyword, in which user interest may be indicated.

First User
A user whose indication of interest in a first advertisement displayed on a parked domain web page is received.<SEP>A user who shows interest in the first advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page.<SEP>A user associated with the parked domain web page, distinct from the second and third users.<SEP>A user seeking to find a second user via a social network; the first user has an identifier, a location, and a social network that can be traversed and combined from multiple social network types.

Second User
A user, different from the first user, whose indication of interest in a second advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page is received.<SEP>A user who shows interest in the second advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page.<SEP>A user whose indication of interest in the second advertisement is received and used to determine the second weight of the second keyword.<SEP>A user whom the first user is trying to find using the social network; the second user has an associated identifier and a possible location.

Third User
A user, different from the first user and the second user, who requests content to provide for display with the parked domain web page.<SEP>A user different from the first and second users who requests content to provide for display with the parked domain web page.<SEP>A user in the first user's social network who is likely to connect the first user's social network with the third user's own social network and whose last-known location is within a predetermined distance from the first user's location; the third user may opt in to sharing identity, social network, or location information.

First Keyword
A keyword of the plurality of keywords having a first weight on the parked domain web page and a different weight on a second information resource.<SEP>A keyword of the plurality of keywords having a first weight on the parked domain web page and a different weight on a second information resource, ranked highest to select the third advertisement.<SEP>A keyword of the plurality of keywords having a first weight on the parked domain web page and a different weight on a second information resource; it is ranked and selected as the highest ranked keyword.

Second Keyword
A keyword of the plurality of keywords associated with the second advertisement, having a second weight determined based on the second user's interest indication.<SEP>A keyword of the plurality of keywords associated with the second advertisement, having a second weight determined based on the second user's interest.<SEP>A keyword of the plurality of keywords associated with a second advertisement, whose second weight is determined based on an indication of user interest.

Third Keyword
A keyword of the plurality of keywords associated with the third advertisement of the parked domain web page.<SEP>A keyword of the plurality of keywords associated with the third advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page.

Unique Identifier
An identifier associated with a parked domain web page, used to identify keywords and associate weights.<SEP>An identifier of the parked domain web page used to identify keywords of advertisements from the database.

User Interest Indication
An indication of user interest in an advertisement, including at least one of a click, a selection, a finger gesture, a mouse over, and a conversion.<SEP>An indication of a user's interest in an advertisement, including at least one of a click, a selection, a finger gesture, a mouse over, and a conversion.

Click
A user interaction constituting an indication of user interest in an advertisement.

Conversion
A user interaction constituting an indication of user interest in an advertisement.

Historic Performance
Past performance on the parked domain web page of keywords corresponding to user interest of users other than the first user, used in determining keyword weights.<SEP>Past performance of keywords on the parked domain web page corresponding to user interest of users other than the first user, used in determining keyword weights.

Content Request
A request received from a user for content to provide for display with the parked domain web page.

Keyword Ranking
The process of ranking keywords based on their weights to select a highest ranked keyword for content selection.

Content Selection
The process of selecting content, such as an advertisement, to provide for display with an information resource based on selected keywords or their weights.

Second Information Resource
An information resource on which the first keyword has a different weight than on the parked domain web page.

Characteristic
An attribute associated with user interest used in determining keyword weights, including temporal, day, web page content slot, monetary, and performance characteristics.<SEP>Attributes of e-mail exchanges between pairs of users, including interaction frequency, interaction type, number of communication participants, time between interactions, time since first interaction, time since last interaction, interaction volume, and ratio of source to target versus target to source interactions.

User Interaction
An interaction by a user with an advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page, used to assign keyword weights.

Threshold Weight
A weight value that a highest weighted keyword must satisfy for selection.

Computer Network
A network via which the system evaluates information.<SEP>A network over which requests, recommendations, and scores are transmitted between content sites, the personalization network service, and external recommenders.<SEP>A network over which requests from content sites for item recommendations are received.

Non-Transitory Computer Readable Medium
A medium having instructions to evaluate information, comprising instructions to perform the described operations.<SEP>A computer readable medium storing instructions, referenced in claim 18 and claim 19.<SEP>A medium containing executable instructions that when executed perform a method of generating relationship data.<SEP>A medium containing executable instructions that when executed perform a method of modeling relationships between e-mail users.

First Weight
The weight of the first keyword on the parked domain web page, used in ranking the first keyword against the second keyword.

Second Weight
The weight of the second keyword determined based on the indication of user interest of the second user in the second advertisement.

Indication Of User Interest
A signal indicating the second user's interest in the second advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page.

Request For Content
A request from the third user for content to provide for display with the parked domain web page.

US9118735B1
A patent document titled "Finding people using social networks" that describes embodiments, a system, and a method for assisting a first person in finding a second person using social networks, including privacy mechanisms such as anonymizing identifying information and encrypting communications.

Requesting Person
A person who sends a request to a server identifying himself or herself, the person being sought, and the requestor's location, in order to find a target person using a social network.

Target Person
The second person whom the requesting person is trying to find through the social network.

Connecting Person
A person in the requesting person's social network who is likely to connect the requesting person's social network with the target person's social network and who has a last-known location within a predetermined distance from the requesting person's location.

Social Network
A network of relationships among people, comprising information from at least one social network service, used to connect a requesting person with a target person.<SEP>A network of users associated with the first user that can be determined, traversed, pruned, and combined from different types of social networks to identify connecting users.

Social Network Service
A service that provides social network information used to determine a person's social network.

Privacy Mechanism
Disclosed mechanisms for protecting privacy, including anonymizing identifying information and encrypting communications.

Opt-In
A connecting person's consent to share information about his or her identity, social network, or location with people of at least as many degrees of separation as the number of degrees of separation for the type of relationship involved.<SEP>A user's consent to share information about his or her identity, social network, or location with users of at least as many degrees of separation as the number of degrees of separation for the type of relationship.

Degrees Of Separation
A measure of the number of intermediary connections between two people in a social network, associated with a type of relationship.<SEP>A measure of the number of connections between users, such as the first user and third user, that determines the type of relationship and opt-in sharing requirements.

Last-Known Location
The most recent location determined for a person, which may be based on a wireless network, a geolocation provided by a computer, a venue, or an event the person has identified himself or herself as being at.

Predetermined Distance
A threshold distance from the requesting person's location within which a connecting person's last-known location must fall.<SEP>A distance threshold within which the third user's last-known location must be from the location of the first user.

Wireless Network
A network to which a connecting person's computer is connected, used to determine the last-known location of the connecting person.

Geolocation
Location information provided by a connecting person's computer, used to determine the last-known location of the connecting person.<SEP>A geographic location provided by a computer of a user, such as the third user, used to determine proximity to the first user's location.

Venue
A place that a connecting person has identified himself or herself as being at, used to determine the last-known location.<SEP>A place that a user, such as the third user, has identified himself or herself as being at, which may match the first user's location.

Event
An occurrence that a connecting person has identified himself or herself as being at, used to determine the last-known location.<SEP>An occurrence that a user, such as the third user, has identified himself or herself as being at, which may be the same event as the first user's location.<SEP>A condition registered for monitoring with regard to a history object, triggered when stored information describing an ETL process's performance satisfies specified criteria, causing a subscribed ETL process to be performed.<SEP>An event registered for monitoring with regard to the history object, triggered when the performance of the first ETL process satisfies criteria, and subscribed to by the second ETL process.

Second Connecting Person
An additional person, also referred to as a fourth user, who is likely to connect the requesting person's social network with the target person's social network and whose response may be combined with the connecting person's response.

Common Format
A unified format to which responses from the computers of the connecting person and the second connecting person are converted before being combined.

Fourth User
A user who may connect the first and third users, and whose identifier or response may be withheld based on negative affinity with the first user or an outdated last-known location.

Kiosk
A device having a pre-determined location at which the identifier associated with the first user may be received.

Non-Transitory Computer-Readable Storage Medium
A storage medium bearing computer-executable instructions that, when executed on a computer, cause the computer to perform operations for assisting a first user in finding a second user using a social network.

Token
A replacement value used to anonymize results by replacing an identifier associated with the second user.<SEP>A unit of the input query to which a label is assigned.<SEP>A segment of a query in the first language containing one or more terms, associated with components of the first query pattern and annotated with labels.

Negative Affinity
A relationship condition between the first user and a fourth user that causes a determination not to return the fourth user's identifier.

Threshold Amount Of Time
A time limit used to determine whether a fourth user's last-known location is too old, causing the withholding of the fourth user's identifier or response.

Anonymized Results
Results produced by replacing an identifier associated with the second user with a token and encrypting the results.

Identifier
A value associated with a user, such as a name, image, location, or relationship, used to identify and determine social networks and users.

Recommendation Engine For Social Networks
A patented recommendation engine (US8095432B1) that generates ranked recommendation lists for items based on relationship proximity between members of a social networking utility.

Social Networking Utility
A social network platform within which members are friends or non-friends of an inquiring member, and within which items can be searched and recommendations obtained.<SEP>A social network platform in which members have friends, non-friends, groups, and networks, and through which items can be searched, recommended, and purchased.

Inquiring Member
A member of the social networking utility who requests a search for an item, receives a recommendation list, and has friends and non-friends within the utility.<SEP>A member of the social networking utility who requests searches, receives recommendation lists, and may purchase items or share recommendations.

First Member
A member of the social networking utility who is a friend of the inquiring member and provides a first recommendation for the item; shares a plurality of interests in common with the inquiring member.<SEP>A member of the social networking utility who is a friend of the inquiring member and provides a first recommendation for an item.

Second Member
A member of the social networking utility who is a non-friend of the inquiring member and provides a second recommendation for the item.<SEP>A member of the social networking utility who is a non-friend of the inquiring member and provides a second recommendation for an item.

Third Member
A member of the social networking utility who has a plurality of different interests than the inquiring member and provides a third recommendation for the item.<SEP>A member of the social networking utility who has different interests than the inquiring member and provides a third recommendation, and who may also be a third friend receiving recommendations.

Relationship Proximity
A measure of closeness between a recommending member and the inquiring member, used to rank recommendations.<SEP>A measure of closeness between members within the social networking utility, closest for friends and farthest for strangers, used to rank recommendations.

Recommendation
An opinion or endorsement of an item provided by a member of the social networking utility.<SEP>A suggestion sent to a user to play a second video content feature based on the relationship score.<SEP>A generated suggestion presented to another user for content or characters, based on preferences and relationship scores.

Recommendation List
A generated list for the item comprising the first and second recommendations, with the first recommendation placed higher than the second based on the first rank exceeding the second rank.<SEP>A ranked list of recommendations for an item generated for the inquiring member, ordered by relationship proximity.

Item
A product or object that can be recommended, searched for, tagged, priced, and purchased within the social networking utility.

Processor
The term "Processor" refers to a hardware component or computing element that executes software programs and performs a wide range of computational and operational tasks across various system contexts. As a hardware component, the processor executes applications—such as a recommendation application—and carries out the core operations of a system. In the context of recommendation systems, it is used to determine relationship proximities, rank recommendations, and generate recommendation lists. It also performs computational steps such as clustering and estimating within various methods.

The processor may be a component of a network device, where it is operative to perform actions including first and second pass analyses and purging a classification model. When executing software programs, the processor is operable to perform steps such as receiving, extracting, and storing management data, as well as receiving data-streams, extracting management data, and storing it in a searchable format. In some configurations, the processor is caused by a software program to carry out actions such as receiving, extracting, and storing. It may also be a hardware component that performs the steps of establishing user relationships and executing a filtration method. Additionally, the processor can be coupled to memory and programmed by program code stored in that memory to implement the modules of an apparatus.<SEP>One or more processors in the system configured to interact with a computer-readable medium to perform the described operations.<SEP>At least one processor in a system that executes program instructions to implement the data catalog.<SEP>A component that generates relationship data by determining relationship strength associated with each pair of users.<SEP>A processor that generates relationship data by determining a relationship strength associated with each pair of users.<SEP>A component in communication with memory for executing stored instructions.

Memory

The content of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.

Message State
A state of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.

US9374411B1
A patent document titled "Content recommendations using deep data" that discloses various embodiments for recommending content for users based on character preferences and relationship scores.

Content Recommendation System
A system and method for recommending network content to users by associating a user preferred character with a recommended character via a library and relationship score.

Preferred Character
A character represented in a first network content feature that a user has expressed a preference toward, represented by a corresponding first cast member.

Recommended Character
A character represented in a second network content feature identified via a library based on the user preferred character, represented by a corresponding second cast member.<SEP>A character identified from the library based on the user preferred character and interaction data, represented in a second network content.

Library
A data structure that associates preferred characters to recommended characters according to a relationship score.<SEP>A library that associates a user preferred character to a recommended character according to a relationship score.

Relationship Score
A score calculated based at least in part upon a proportion of users who have expressed a preference towards both the preferred character and the recommended character, quantifying commonality between characters.<SEP>A score calculated based on the proportion of users who expressed a preference toward both the first and second characters, quantifying commonality between characters.<SEP>A score calculated based at least in part on the quantity of users expressing preference toward the first fictional character and on whether the two fictional characters are associated with a similar genre.

First Video Content Feature
A video content feature streamed from a server to a client and rendered in a user interface, containing scenes and cast members including the preferred character.<SEP>A video content feature associated with at least one scene in which a first character is identified.

Second Video Content Feature
A video content feature containing a recommended character, recommended to the user for playback.

Client
A computing device associated with a user that renders video content features and user interfaces and provides user interaction data.<SEP>A client device on which content is displayed and from which user interaction data is obtained.

Timeline User Interface
A user interface that segments a video content feature into a plurality of scenes and includes character feedback interfaces.<SEP>A user interface that segments the first network content into a plurality of scenes and renders character feedback interfaces.

Character Feedback Interface
An interface rendered on the timeline user interface associated with a current scene, through which users provide interaction data about characters.<SEP>An interface rendered on the timeline user interface, associated with a current scene, through which users provide interaction data about characters.

User Interaction Data
Data obtained from a client based on user interactions with video content features and character feedback interfaces, used to determine character preferences.<SEP>Data obtained from a client based on user interactions with content, used to associate users with preferred characters and update relationship scores.

First Cast Member
A cast member of the first video content feature who represents the preferred character.

Second Cast Member
A cast member of the second video content feature who represents the recommended character.

Scene
A segment of a video content feature within the plurality of scenes segmented by the timeline user interface.<SEP>A segment of network content within the plurality of scenes presented on the timeline user interface.

Attribute
A characteristic associated with a recommended character that can be sent to the client to indicate a basis for the recommendation.

Consumption History Data
Data relating to a product associated with a character, used as user interaction data to determine character preferences.

Browse History Data
Data relating to browsing of a product associated with a character, used as user interaction data to determine character preferences.

First Character
A character identified in at least one scene of the first video content feature, toward which users may express a preference.

Second Character
A character toward which users may express a preference, related to the first character via a relationship score.

First Network Content
Network content rendered in a user interface in which a user preferred character is represented.

User Preferred Character
A character represented in the first network content that a user is associated with as preferring, based on interaction data.

Second Network Content
Network content in which the recommended character is represented, for which a recommendation is sent.

Fictional Character
A preferred or recommended character that is fictional, associated with media content.

Electronic Book
An e-book form of media content that may comprise the second network content or first media content.<SEP>A digital book format that the first media content may comprise, as specified in claim 22.

Audio Book
An audio book form of media content that may comprise the second network content.

Explicit User Feedback
Feedback explicitly expressing that a user favors a preferred character, obtained via a user interface.

First Media Content
Media content rendered in a user interface with which a first fictional character is associated.<SEP>Media content referenced in claim 22, which may comprise an electronic book (e-book).

Second Media Content
Media content with which a second fictional character is associated.

First Set Of Attributes
A set of attributes associated with the user preferred character, stored for comparison.

Second Set Of Attributes
A set of attributes associated with the recommended character, stored for comparison.

Computer Instructions
A plurality of computer instructions stored on the medium that cause the computing device to perform various operations, including obtaining user feedback and calculating relationship scores.

First Fictional Character
A fictional character that a user may favor, and whose relationship with a second fictional character is scored.

Second Fictional Character
A fictional character whose relationship with the first fictional character is evaluated and scored.

Genre
A category or classification with which the first and second fictional characters may be associated, used in calculating the relationship score.

Query Parser Derivation Computing Device
A computing device that derives a query parser, assigns labels to tokens, calculates the most probable label sequence, constructs phrase level grammar, and computes conditional probabilities for parsing queries.<SEP>A computing device that derives a query parser for parsing unstructured geographic web-search queries into a field-based format.

Query Parser
A parser derived by the query parser derivation computing device that parses unstructured geographic web-search queries into a field-based format using conditional random fields.<SEP>A derived parser for parsing an unstructured geographic web-search query into a field-based format.

Unstructured Geographic Web-Search Query
An unstructured local geographical web-based query in a local domain that is parsed to produce structured information.<SEP>An unstructured search query of a geographic nature that is parsed into a field-based format.<SEP>A web-search query with geographic intent that is unstructured and comprises a series of tokens.

Conditional Random Fields
A statistical modeling method learned by semi-supervised automated learning and used to parse structured information from unstructured geographic web-search queries.

Semi-Supervised Automated Learning
An automated learning approach by which the conditional random fields are learned.<SEP>A learning approach by which conditional random fields are learned.

Rule-Based Finite State Machine Model
A model used to establish semi-supervised conditional random fields, utilized with a phrase level grammar to construct a phrase level grammar composition.<SEP>One of the models that may be used to establish the semi-supervised conditional random fields.

Statistics-Based Conditional Random Field Model
A model used to establish semi-supervised conditional random fields, utilized with class transition features learned from a labeled set of features and high-level language models as state features.<SEP>One of the models that may be used to establish the semi-supervised conditional random fields.

Systematic Geographic Parsing
A parsing technique used with the rule-based finite state machine model or the statistics-based conditional random field model to establish the semi-supervised conditional random fields.

Learned Model Parser
A parser based on training that is applied to the query, using class-based query logs and class-level multi-token language model-based features.<SEP>A parser applied to an unstructured local geographical web-based query in a local domain, comprising at least one class-level n-gram language model-based feature.

Class-Based Query Log
A log from a form-based query system used by the learned model parser, comprising a structured query log.<SEP>A query log from a form-based query system used in applying the learned model parser to a query.

Form-Based Query System
A query system that provides the class-based query log.

Class-Level N-Gram Language Model-Based Feature
A feature harvested from a structured query log and comprised by the learned model parser.

Structured Query Log
A log from which the class-level n-gram language model-based feature is harvested.

Input Query
A query comprising a series of tokens, to which labels are assigned and for which the most probable label sequence is calculated.<SEP>A query received as input that comprises a series of tokens.

Tokens
The series of tokens comprising the input query, to which labels are assigned.<SEP>Segments of a given query in the first language, each including one or more terms from the query.

Labels
Labels assigned to tokens of the input query, corresponding to a search term, geographic expression, geographic expression relation indication, and/or uninteresting information.<SEP>Labels assigned to tokens of the input query, identifying them as corresponding to a search term, a geographic expression, a geographic expression relation indication, and/or uninteresting information.<SEP>Annotations identifying the parts of each query, associated with corresponding components of the first query pattern.

Most Probable Label Sequence
The calculated most probable sequence of labels for the input query.

Sentences
Sentences assigned to each label based on the most probable label sequence, different from the labels, identifying the respective label.<SEP>Sentences assigned to each label based at least in part on the most probable label sequence, different from the labels.

Feature Functions
A set of functions fk each having a corresponding weight λk, representing state transition features and output state features for a given input sequence.<SEP>A set of one or more feature functions representing a state transition feature and/or features of an output state for an input sequence, used to compute a conditional probability.

State Transition Feature
A feature function representing transitions between states, including fk(lt−1, lt, Q), trained on a labeled set.<SEP>A feature representing a state transition, trained on a labeled set with learning limited relative to learning the output state features.<SEP>A feature representing transitions between states, trained on a labeled set with learning limited relative to output state features.

Output State Features
One or more features of an output state for an input sequence, trained on a labeled set.

Labeled Set
A set of labeled data on which the state transition features and output state features are trained.<SEP>A set of labeled data used to train state transition and output state features.

Structured Information
Information produced by parsing the unstructured geographic web-search query.<SEP>Information produced from the unstructured geographic web-search query by utilizing the conditional random fields.<SEP>Information produced from the unstructured geographic web-search query via conditional random fields.

Multiple Interpretation Condition
A condition resulting from parsing the unstructured geographic web-search query that identifies a first interpretation and a second interpretation.<SEP>A condition in which parsing the unstructured geographic web-search query results in multiple interpretations.<SEP>A condition where parsing the query identifies a first interpretation and a second interpretation with corresponding parsing results.

First Interpretation
A first interpretation of the unstructured geographic web-search query corresponding to first parsing results.<SEP>One interpretation of the unstructured geographic web-search query corresponding to first parsing results.

Second Interpretation
A second interpretation of the unstructured geographic web-search query corresponding to second parsing results.<SEP>Another interpretation of the unstructured geographic web-search query corresponding to second parsing results.

First Parsing Results
Parsing results corresponding to the first interpretation of the unstructured geographic web-search query.<SEP>Parsing results corresponding to the first interpretation of the query.

Second Parsing Results
Parsing results corresponding to the second interpretation of the unstructured geographic web-search query.<SEP>Parsing results corresponding to the second interpretation of the query.

User Behavior Data
Data used to disambiguate first parsing results and second parsing results to select the first parsing results.<SEP>Data used to disambiguate the first parsing results and the second parsing results.<SEP>Data used to disambiguate between parsing results and select an interpretation.

Class-Based Language Model Features
Features comprising at least one token appearing in a defined position in a model feature comprising a grouping of tokens of a given length n.

GEO_UNI_FIRST
A class-based language model feature for the first token in a grouping of tokens of length one relating to a geographic term.

GEO_BI_FIRST
A class-based language model feature for the first token in a grouping of tokens of length two relating to a geographic term.

GEO_BI_SECOND
A class-based language model feature for the second token in a grouping of tokens of length two relating to a geographic term.

GEO_TRI_FIRST
A class-based language model feature for the first token in a grouping of tokens of length three relating to a geographic term.

GEO_TRI_SECOND
A class-based language model feature for the second token in a grouping of tokens of length three relating to a geographic term.

GEO_TRI_THIRD
A class-based language model feature for the third token in a grouping of tokens of length three relating to a geographic term.

ST_UNI_FIRST
A class-based language model feature for the first token in a grouping of tokens of length one relating to a search term.

ST_BI_FIRST
A class-based language model feature for the first token in a grouping of tokens of length two relating to a search term.

ST_BI_SECOND
A class-based language model feature for the second token in a grouping of tokens of length two relating to a search term.

ST_TRI_FIRST
A class-based language model feature for the first token in a grouping of tokens of length three relating to a search term.

ST_TRI_SECOND
A class-based language model feature for the second token in a grouping of tokens of length three relating to a search term.

ST_TRI_THIRD
A class-based language model feature for the third token in a grouping of tokens of length three relating to a search term.

Semi-Supervised Conditional Random Fields
A statistical model established via a rule-based finite state machine model or a statistics-based conditional random field model, used for labeling and parsing query tokens.

Phrase Level Grammar
A grammar used with the rule-based finite state machine model to construct a phrase level grammar composition, constructed using a context free grammar composition.

Context Free Grammar Composition
A grammar composition used by the query parser derivation computing device to construct the phrase level grammar.

Linear-Chain Markov Random Field Model
A model in which the semi-supervised conditional random fields are utilized.

Conditional Random Field Model
A model of Q and L characterized as a set of feature functions each having a corresponding weight, with a computed conditional probability.<SEP>A model created based on tokens, labels, and feature functions, used to produce structured information from unstructured queries.

Output State Feature
A feature function representing features of an output state, including fk(lt, Q), for a given input sequence.<SEP>Features of an output state for an input sequence, trained on a labeled set.

Class-Level Multi-Token Language Model-Based Feature
A feature harvested from a structured query log and used by the learned model parser.

A parser comprised by the learned model parser that performs segmenting and labeling query sequence data.

Non-Transitory Machine-Readable Media
Media having machine-readable instructions that, when executed by computing devices, cause the devices to derive a query parser for parsing an unstructured geographic web-search query into a field-based format.<SEP>Media having machine-readable instructions that, when executed, cause computing devices to perform operations.

A format into which the query parser parses an unstructured geographic web-search query.

Label
A classification assigned to tokens, corresponding to a search term, a geographic expression, a geographic expression relation indication, and/or uninteresting information.<SEP>An annotation applied to tokens of a query identifying the parts of the query and corresponding to components of the first query pattern.

Sentences assigned to each label that identify the label as corresponding to a search term, geographic expression, geographic expression relation indication, and/or uninteresting information.
